items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Robert La Gamma invited us to Thanksgiving dinner along with Monsieur and Madame Pango the 25th.

ctx.x: The next exciting thing in the travels of my horn and me happened the 21st of November, 1971, when I was engaged to go to West Africa. It came through the U.S. Cultural Center's African programming office. My wife and I left Paris (Orly airport) the night of November 21st at 10:35 on an African airline plane, and arrived at Abidjan airport in the Ivory Coast at 5 o'clock in the morning of the 22nd. I had been in North Africa quite a number of times, but never in other parts of Africa, so naturally, I was excited…

The assistant director of the U.S. Cultural Center, a young man from Boston named Robert La Gamma, his wife and the director of the National Orchestra of the Ivory Coast, a Monsieur Jean-Joseph Pango, met us at the air-port and these personalities gave us the feeling that we were going to enjoy our stay in Abidjan. We had no idea of what to expect in a part of the world; we had never visited before, but when the time came for us to leave, we knew that we would never forget that country and the wonderful people we…

I was engaged to play three concerts within eight days. It was a mysterious deal from the first time I learned that I was to play with a big band because the U.S. Cultural Center's director in Paris could never get any information about the composition of the orchestra.
